links.outcome: Prospective silent-mode diagnostic performance for DME detection on live patients
links.effect: In silent mode (603 patients), sensitivity 98.8% (95% CI, 94.5%-100.0%) and specificity 90.7% (95% CI, 88.7%-92.4%); 7.2% scans ungradable, 4.4% uncertain.
links.quote: The system achieved 98.8% (95% CI, 94.5%-100.0%) sensitivity and 90.7% (95% CI, 88.7%-92.4%) specificity for DME detection.

openai.sample_unit: patients (603 in prospective silent-mode validation; 276 in the randomized trial)

links.outcome: DME referral sensitivity using AI-OCT as an adjunct to fundus screening
links.effect: DME referral sensitivity was 100.0% (95% CI, 100.0%-100.0%) in both groups. No DME occurred among nonreferred intervention participants.
links.quote: Compared with standard practice, incorporation of the AI-OCT system as a secondary screening tool was noninferior with respect to false-positive referral rates and was associated with a substantial reduction in potentially unnecessary DME referrals without compromising sensitivity.

links.outcome: False-positive DME referrals versus standard screening
links.effect: False-positive referral rates were 24.1% versus 69.1%; absolute difference, -45% (95% CI, -58.2% to -31.9%; P < .001 for noninferiority). All participants ultimately underwent specialist evaluation.
links.quote: The false-positive DME referral rate was 24.1% (95% CI, 14.6%-37.0%) and 69.1% (95% CI, 61.0%-76.1%), respectively (absolute difference, -45% [95% CI, -58.2% to -31.9%; P < .001 for noninferiority]; upper bound of the CI below the prespecified noninferiority margin of 20%).

links.effect: The false-positive DME referral rate was 24.1% in the intervention group and 69.1% in the control group.
links.quote: The false-positive DME referral rate was 24.1% (95% CI, 14.6%-37.0%) and 69.1% (95% CI, 61.0%-76.1%), respectively (absolute difference, -45% [95% CI, -58.2% to -31.9%; P < .001 for noninferiority]; upper bound of the CI below the prespecified noninferiority margin of 20%).
